questions.prompt: Week 28 · Conservatism, Reagan, and the End of the Cold War: What is the strongest method for evaluating “Why Did the Cold War End?”?
choices: Accept the source because it was created during the period.
Reject the source if it has a perspective or purpose.
Compare it with independent evidence and evaluate origin, purpose, context, value, and limits.
Use only the most memorable statement.
questions.explanation: Historical evidence is evaluated through sourcing, contextualization, corroboration, and attention to limitations.

questions.prompt: A table compares tax rates, inflation, unemployment, union membership, defense spending, and federal deficits across the 1980s. What is the strongest approach?
choices: Evaluate each policy claim against the relevant measure and time period, distinguish correlation from causation, and examine who experienced gains or costs.
Use whichever indicator changed most to judge every policy outcome.
Treat national averages as proof that every group experienced the decade similarly.
Assume any two trends moving together have the same cause.
questions.explanation: Policy evaluation requires matching claims to appropriate measures, examining distribution, and avoiding simple correlation-equals-causation reasoning.

shortResponse.prompt: Using at least two specific pieces of evidence, answer: Why did modern conservatism gain power, and what caused the Cold War to end?
